brief: Morgan Stanley sales commentary. The micro kept returning to AI: Oracle cloud infrastructure revenue rose 121% to $7.4B, TSMC August revenue rose 53.3% year over year, Meta launched its Muse consumer agent, and Quality buying broadened beyond Tech into Healthcare, Financials and higher-end Consumer with re-grossing still light. Macro carried the week. Brent moved back above $100/bbl on Middle East escalation, which with an underwhelming Treasury buyback pushed the US 10Y to its highest level since October 2023 and the 30Y to its highest since 2007. Friday's CPI printed firmer than expected but still showed disinflation, so the data arguably still allows a hold, while markets moved September hike odds to nearly 90%, leaving the Fed constrained by pricing rather than by data. Savone reads the move toward higher Quality as an early-to-mid-cycle rotation, not a defensive turn. Prime brokerage data shows funds re-grossing yet net sellers of global equities, with US long/short net leverage down 2ppts to 52% and gross at 208%, near 12-month lows.
